newsitem.title: USA: Brooklyn Union cites further utility growth.
newsitem.headline: Brooklyn Union cites further utility growth.

text.p: Brooklyn Union Gas Co Thursday reported a third quarter, ended June 30, profit citing further growth of its utility operations.
The profit in the latest quarter -- $2.2 million, or $0.04 per share -- compared with a loss of $4.6 million, or nine cents per share, for the third quarter last year.
The third quarter is marginally profitable, or unprofitable due to the seasonal nature of gas heating sales, the company's principal source of revenue, it pointed out.

The utility said the sharply higher third quarter results were primarily due to continued growth in operating results from the gas distribution business, including gas sales growth, added revenue streams from expanded services and attainment of cost efficiencies.
It said regulated gas distribution operations trimmed their loss to $2.8 million, or $0.06 per share, in the quarter from $8.5 million, or $0.17 per share, a year earlier.
Brooklyn Union's energy-related investments group earned $6.1 million, or $0.12 per share, during the latest quarter, compared with $4.3 million, or $0.09 per share, last year.
It said the increase reflected income from investments in exploration and production and gas transmission was offset slightly by losses in cogeneration.
The company noted energy-related investment group plans to participate in a wireless data-communications venture.
It said the energy-marketing group had a loss of $1.1 million, or $0.02 per share, during the quarter and noted they were not in operation a year ago.
Earnings for the nine months ended June 30, were up nine percent, to $127.2 million, or $2.54 per share, from $114.5 million, or $2.33 per share, for the same period a year ago.
Earnings from gas distribution were $117.3 million, or $2.34 per share, compared with $107.5 million, or $2.19 per share during the nine-month period last year.
Brooklyn Union is "on target in achieving most of our customer, operational and financial goals for this year," said Craig Matthews, president and chief operating officer.

Firm gas sales for the nine-month period, which was 1.4 percent warmer than normal, were 121.7 billion cubic feet, compared with 128.4 billion in last year's first nine months, which were 7.7 percent colder than normal.
The energy-related investments group contributed $13.3 million, or $0.27 per share, compared with $6.9 million, or $0.14 per share, last year.
These earnings "are up sharply and reflect the success of our long-term diversification strategies," said Vincent Enright, chief financial officer.
